goal: BRUTALLY critique it against the objective/principles/specification document below. THAT IS THE BIBLE OF WHAT WE WANT TO ACHIEVE (not necessarily exactly HOW) with sisi. Find ALL the flaws, the unnecessary complexities, the things that are just flat out wrong. Consider its use and its customers, what goes in sisi itself (things that work broadly across all projects, all users) versus what is learned and evolved for an individual user. Then convert that into a PLAN and IMPLEMENTATION to fix it. Anything short of perfection, based on that document below, is UNACCEPTABLE!! Please save this spec document VERBATIM in the project. It is our ONE TRUE NORTH STAR!!!

in: the rebuild of sisi to meet the specification, including one generic orchestrator
the switch of the owner's installation and removal of the old orchestrator
out: evidence of improvement over time (SPEC 20.3): only the means to measure it are in scope

risk.why: this changes hooks that run in every session of every tool the owner uses, migrates his personal data, and replaces his installed copy
risk.blast_radius: every agent session on the owner's machine: session start, each prompt, each shell command and the end of each turn; his learned data; his Claude instructions and settings
risk.rollback: sisi rollback switches the installed copy back and the old code runs against the migrated data; the timestamped archive made by the cutover restores the data folder, CLAUDE.md, settings.json and the old orchestrator

approach.chosen: staged reconciliation in the order SPEC 19 gives, each stage built in its own checkout and merged only with the suite passing
approach.why: it keeps what the audits showed is working, removes what serves no requirement, and lets each stage be verified and reviewed on its own
alternatives: rewrite from the specification on a clean slate: loses the safe installer and the hooks that work
patch the missing pieces on top: keeps every duplicate and every unenforced rule
reuses: the contract, check runner and gate
the safe installer and release with rollback

requirements.text: a brutal critique against the specification, naming every flaw and needless complexity
the specification saved verbatim in the project
a plan and an implementation that meet the specification, plus a generic, strategic orchestration layer replacing orch.py
what is product (all projects, all users) is separated from what is learned for one user
the owner's learned data, statements and delegation history survive the switch
requirements.why: a rebuild that loses his data is not an improvement

requirements.text: sessions already running keep working, or he is told to restart them
requirements.why: his installed copy serves every open session

requirements.text: standard library only, no scheduler, nothing in the product naming a model, price or person
he will want to try it on another project before every stage is finished

requirements.why: it needs time; the unit record, scorecard and evaluation harness are what will show it
